svg.title: QP2609 Q4 - D6: WinGD Pulse Jet (Pulse Lubricating System) - functional block diagram, separate maker
svg.desc: A different maker's system, not part of the Everllence installation. Cylinder oil from the service tank or tanks, by gravity or a supply pump - a single validated grade, or two grades with manual changeover valves near the engine inlet - enters at engine inlet 33 through a duplex oil filter to one cylinder lubricating pump per cylinder. Where the optional iCAT automatic changeover is fitted, a second, high-BN inlet 32 with its own filter is added, and the iCAT change-over valve near the pump, after the filters, selects inlet 33 or 32. Servo oil operates the pump; the engine control system commands its solenoid valve and reads a pressure transmitter. Quills with non-return valves inject oil whose distribution above, into and below the ring pack is set by control-system timing parameters. The piston-underside drain is sampled for residual BN and iron and the operator adjusts the feed rate.
svg.text: Q4 - D6 WinGD Pulse Jet / Pulse Lubricating System (PLS) - a DIFFERENT maker's alternative
NOT part of the Everllence B&W installation in D1-D5. Functional blocks only: WinGD does not publish the pump's internal hydraulics.
Cylinder oil supply (MIM options)
service tank(s) by gravity, or a supply
pump from the service tank;
single grade validated for all fuels:
no changeover device, or
two service tanks + manual changeover
valves close to the engine inlet;
trace heating to the engine inlet;
with iCAT: a second (high-BN) inlet
Duplex filter - inlet 33
Duplex filter - inlet 32
inlet 32: high BN, iCAT only
Cylinder lubricating pump - one per cylinder
Solenoid valve
commanded by the engine control system (ECS)
Servo-oil operation
servo oil from a reduced-pressure distributor (mini-rail)
iCAT change-over valve near the pump (option)
after the filters: selects 33 or 32 (no iCAT: 33 feeds the pump)
Dosage pump
cylinder oil to
the quills
Pressure transmitter
feedback to ECS
ECS
adjustable, load-related feed rate;
timing parameters set where the
oil is placed; pre-lubrication
pulses at start
Quills in the liner, each with a non-return valve
nozzle holes and spray angles give jets onto the liner wall;
distribution above / into / below the ring pack is set by
the ECS timing parameters;
grooves spread fresh oil in the upper stroke area
Feed-rate management (WinGD guideline)
BN selected to suit the fuel's total sulphur;
no high-BN oil needed on LNG, methanol
or ammonia; drain oil from the piston
underside at least weekly: residual BN
and iron, on board and by laboratory;
in the "Safe" area reduce in steps to a
minimum, or keep the current rate
Contrast with Everllence B&W (D1-D2)
MAN: oil delivered as the rings pass the quills (into the ring pack).
WinGD: usually mostly above the ring pack, part into it, a little below.
Sources: WinGD Tribology, Fuels & Lubricants web page (Pulse Jet); WinGD Operation Manual X82DF issue 002 (2021) s.4.5-4.6 and Fig 4-6, s.5.7;
WinGD MIM X72DF-1.1 (2021) and X72DF-M-1.0 (2026-07) s.4.3.6 and Figure 4-9; WinGD Lubricants guideline DTAA001621 rev B (25 Nov 2025).
